title: Disaster Recovery
description: Design and test disaster recovery strategies for Linux-based production systems, including backups, restores, and failover procedures.

data.text: Disaster recovery is your insurance policy against data loss, hardware failure, or human error. A tested backup strategy beats an untested one every time. This lesson shows you how to design backups that are frequent, verified, and recoverable.
We will cover Linux backup tools, RPO and RTO objectives, and how to automate restore testing without disrupting production.

Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time. Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the maximum acceptable downtime. Together they define your disaster recovery requirements.

data.title: Watch Out
data.text: If you have never tested a restore, your backup strategy is a hope, not a plan. Schedule restore tests quarterly and document the results.
Linux offers mature tools for file-level and block-level backups. Choose the right tool for your data type and retention requirements.

items: rsync: efficient file sync and incremental backups
tar + gpg: compressed and encrypted archives
Restic: fast, encrypted backups to S3 or local storage

data.title: Automated encrypted backup script
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# Daily encrypted backup of /etc and /var/www

BACKUP_DIR="/var/backups/daily"
DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
PASSPHRASE="$BACKUP_GPG_PASSPHRASE"
export PASSPHRASE

tar czf - /etc /var/www \
  | gpg --batch --passphrase "$PASSPHRASE" -c \
  > "$BACKUP_DIR/backup-$DATE.tar.gz.gpg"

find "$BACKUP_DIR" -type f -mtime +30 -delete

echo "Backup completed: backup-$DATE.tar.gz.gpg"

data.text: Backups protect against data loss. High availability protects against downtime. On Linux, `keepalived`, `Pacemaker`, and cloud load balancers can route traffic away from failed nodes automatically.

items: Deploy redundant instances across availability zones
Use a floating IP or DNS failover mechanism
Test failover by manually killing the primary node
Measure actual RTO during the test
Define RPO and RTO for each service
Automate daily backups with offsite replication
Encrypt backups and store keys separately
Test full restores in a staging environment quarterly
Document failover steps in a runbook

data.title: Summary
data.text: Disaster recovery requires both strong backup tools and regular testing. Define RPO and RTO, automate encrypted backups, and practice failovers in staging. The only bad backup plan is the one you never tested.
